prompt:

- device_troubleshooting: Device or app malfunction not tied to a specific recent software update — data/photos disappearing, hardware defects (headphones, AirPods), iMessage not sending, App Store not loading.
 (examples: All my photos got deleted off my phone help; My AirPods won't pair and keep making a dropping noise; iMessage isn't working, I can't send or receive texts)

 (examples: Battery life is half of what it was since updating to iOS 11; Ever since iOS 11 my WiFi and Bluetooth turn back on by themselves; Why does typing I autocorrect to a box with a question mark)

 (examples: I forgot my Apple ID password and can't recover my account; My iCloud account has been locked for security reasons; Is this email asking to verify my account a phishing scam?)

 (examples: You charged me for an Apple Music subscription I never requested; iTunes won't accept my PayPal as a payment method; I bought an album but it won't let me redownload it)
- repair_order_status: Pre-order/order status, activation, and warranty questions for a device purchase — largely iPhone X launch-period order tracking.
 (examples: My iPhone X order says preparing for shipment, is that normal?; iPhone X won't activate, activation servers are down; Does my unlocked iPhone warranty apply internationally?)
- general_complaint: Dissatisfaction with a product redesign, in-store experience, or customer-support interaction, without a specific fixable bug report.
 (examples: The new Podcasts app redesign is unusable, please revert it; Had the worst customer service experience at the Apple Store; AppleCare support wasted 90 minutes and fixed nothing)
- feature_how_to: "How do I" / "where is this feature" questions about something that exists but the customer can't find or hasn't figured out yet.
 (examples: I updated to iOS 11.2 but don't see Apple Pay Cash, how do I enable it?; How do I set up Apple Pay Cash in Wallet settings?; Where did the option to add a card in Wallet go?)

as a careful Tier-1 support agent making a judgment call. Follow this rubric
exactly.

Intents (pick exactly one):
- device_troubleshooting: Device or app malfunction not tied to a specific recent software update — data/photos disappearing, hardware defects (headphones, AirPods), iMessage not sending, App Store not loading.
- software_update_bug: A bug the customer attributes directly to an OS/app update — battery drain after updating, the iOS 11 "I" autocorrect glitch, Bluetooth/ WiFi re-enabling itself, a Mac bricked by a High Sierra update.
- apple_id_account_access: Locked out of or unable to verify an Apple ID / iCloud account, plus questions about whether an Apple-branded email is a phishing attempt (account-security adjacent).
- billing_subscription: Charges, payment methods, or subscription/purchase access issues — primarily Apple Music/iTunes billing and purchased-content access.
- repair_order_status: Pre-order/order status, activation, and warranty questions for a device purchase — largely iPhone X launch-period order tracking.
- general_complaint: Dissatisfaction with a product redesign, in-store experience, or customer-support interaction, without a specific fixable bug report.
- feature_how_to: "How do I" / "where is this feature" questions about something that exists but the customer can't find or hasn't figured out yet.
- positive_feedback: Short acknowledgment that a fix worked or thanks for help — closing messages in an already-resolved thread.
- out_of_scope: HDBSCAN noise, plus low-content/meta-conversational traffic that isn't a standalone actionable support message on its own: bare "help me" with no content, "check DM"/"sent a DM", "same issue" with no restated context, bare version-number replies, emoji-only replies, and non-English text (English-only scope per PRD 7).

- escalate: the issue needs account-specific action the brand can't do in a
  public/templated reply, the customer is visibly upset after repeated
  contact, there's any safety/legal/financial-harm language, or the "right"
  reply isn't obvious from precedent.
- auto_handle: the issue is a known, templatable fix (password reset link,
  standard troubleshooting step, FAQ-style answer) and the customer's tone
  doesn't suggest they're already frustrated.
